recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add Binary.securityContext as a Patient compartment search parameter without a new work-group decision, because the later FHIR-22269/FHIR-51725 path deliberately distinguishes formal computable membership from access-control treatment of Binary.
issue_request: FHIR-26879 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked that Binary not be excluded from the Patient compartment, specifically for Binary resources whose securityContext points to the patient.
initial_application: No commit explicitly tagged FHIR-26879 was found. The contemporaneous Zulip thread identified the old exclusion as a tooling artifact, and the Jira issue was later annotated "see 22269".
additional_context: FHIR-22269 later revisited the same Binary/compartment question and changed the implementation strategy: remove the old never-list wording and add guidance that resources outside formal compartments can still be relevant for access control, using Binary as the example. FHIR-51725 later clarified that listed resources with .param elements are formal compartment members and listed resources without .param elements are outside the compartment, while non-compartment resources can still be returned by _include or local convention.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active CompartmentDefinition narrative and compartment page template already address the seed concern without adding Binary.securityContext as a Patient compartment search parameter.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive with Modification issue that supplied the applied source strategy for the same Binary/compartment concern.
Later Applied clarification that resources listed without .param elements are outside the formal compartment but may still be returned or handled by local convention.
